Motion AI · 5-4 · Emergency mission

From Words to Motion — Placing Words and Gestures on the Same Map

In 5-3, a motion became a point made of 16 numbers. This time, words become points too. We train a text funnel and a motion funnel together so that the sentence "손을 흔든다" (waves a hand) and the hand-waving motion land on the same spot of the same map. Watch the lines, tangled at first, find their partners as training goes on, and at the end type a sentence to make the stick figure move. Even the single word "춤춰" (Dance!) becomes a motion here for the first time.

2Words are numbers

Words are numbers too — a 40-slot bag of words

Type a sentence or click an example. Of the 40 word pieces in the dictionary, only those found in the sentence become 1. These 40 numbers are the input to the text funnel.

Explanation for beginners

A bag of words sees a sentence only as "which words are in it". It throws away word order, particles and context. So "버린" (threw away) in "길에 캔을 던져 버린다" (throws a can away on the street) and "버린" in "쓰레기통에 쓰레기를 버린다" (throws trash into the bin) switch on the same slot — even though one is littering and the other is normal. This crudeness shows up as real mistakes in Section 6. Ways to put a sentence’s order and context into numbers as well are covered in 3-5 and 3-8.

The training on screen above re-runs the same computation in the browser (with different random numbers), so the numbers at each step differ slightly. 5 of the 7 test sentences found their own motion. The 2 that did not are examined in Section 6.

What does contrastive learning fix?

  1. Pick one scene and one sentence for each kind. That makes 7 pairs.
  2. Fold the 7 sentences with the text funnel (40 → 8) and the 7 scenes with the motion funnel (the 16 numbers from 5-3 → 8).
  3. Multiply the two (dot product) to make a 7 × 7 score table. The diagonal holds the true pairs.
  4. Turn each row and each column into probabilities with softmax, and nudge the weights of both funnels so the diagonal probabilities move toward 1. Repeat this 400 times.

CLIP [R1], which aligns words and images this way, and MotionCLIP [R2], which aligns words and motions, work on the same principle. Real models use a transformer as the text funnel and hundreds of millions of pairs.

4Same map

Words and motions on the same map

The points on the 8-slot map were scaled to length 1 (so only direction counts) and then flattened onto the two directions in which they spread the most. Circles are motion scenes, diamonds are sentences. Move the training step from 0 to 400 and see whether each sentence moves next to its own cluster of motions.

Training step400

After training, circles (motions) and diamonds (sentences) of the same color gather together. Words and motions now live in "the same neighborhood of the same map". Now, if you put one sentence on the map, you can pull out a motion near it or draw a new motion from that neighborhood.

5Words → motion

Type a sentence and the stick figure moves

Type a sentence and press Enter. "Find" pulls out the nearest scene on the map as is, and "Make" draws a new motion from the spot where the 5 nearest scenes gather. Join two sentences with "~다가" (while …) or "~고 나서" (after …) and the two motions are stitched one after the other.

Mode

Results of Code 2 — is the generated motion really that kind?

Mode21 training sentences (×5 each)7 test sentences (×5 each)
Find100.0%71.4%
Make100.0%71.4%

The kind of each generated motion was judged by which kind’s center is nearest in the 5-3 latent space. "춤춰" (Dance!) → the generated motion was judged as dancing, with a bone-length error of 5.4%. Stitching: "걸어가다가 손을 흔든다" (waves a hand while walking) → first half walking past · second half waving; "손을 흔들고 나서 춤춰" (wave, and then dance!) → waving · dancing; "캔을 줍고 쓰레기통에 넣는다" (picks up a can and puts it in the bin) → picking up · putting in the bin.

To make "Make" better

In this part, "Make" approximates the spot where the five nearest scenes on the map gather with a mean and a spread, and unfolds it with the linear decoder from 5-3. Real text-to-motion models instead use diffusion models that take the sentence as a condition and strip noise away to reveal a motion (MDM [R4]), or turn motion into tokens and keep writing the next token (T2M-GPT [R5]). For training data, HumanML3D [R3], in which people wrote sentences for every motion, is widely used.

6Limits

Where the bag of words fails, and the final mission

2 of the 7 test sentences found the wrong motion. In both cases the reason is clear.

Test sentenceCorrect answerMotions found (5 nearest)Why it failed
"길에 캔을 던져 버린다" (throws a can away on the street)Throw farputting in the bin × 5"던져" (throw) is a piece that never appeared in the training sentences, and "버린" (threw away) is a piece learned from a binning sentence ("쓰레기통에 쓰레기를 버린다", throws trash into the bin). Without context, it got dragged toward "버린다 = binning"
"손을 펴서 떨어뜨리고 걸어간다" (opens the hand, drops it and walks away)Drop at feetwalking past × 5"걸어" (walk) and "간다" (goes) pulled hard toward walking past. A bag of words does not know which word is the main action (dropping)
"걷다가 손 흔들기" (walking, then waving) (Section 5)walking past → wavingFirst half is wrong"걷" (walk) is in the dictionary but never appeared in a training sentence (the training sentences all use "걸어"). A slot that was never learned does not point anywhere on the map

The "Motions found" in the table above are the results of Code 1. In Section 5, which re-trains in the browser, "길에 캔을 던져 버린다" (throws a can away on the street) sometimes goes toward picking up instead. Where it gets dragged depends on the random numbers in training, but the reason it cannot find throwing (a bag of words that does not know context) stays the same.

What we learned in this part
  • Words become points too: turn a sentence into numbers and fold it with a funnel, and it lands on the same map as motions.
  • Learning from pairs: contrastive learning aligns two funnels with nothing but "partners close, strangers far". Loss 1.90 → 0.01.
  • Pull out and draw from the map: find and make, plus stitching in sentence order.
Open problems
  • The text funnel is too shallow: handling order, context and unseen words takes a text encoder such as a transformer (3-8).
  • A stick figure is still a stick figure: we made it dance, but it is still just a skeleton. Dressing this skeleton in a person’s (the Assistant’s) appearance and turning it into a video is the final mission.
the DoctorWith the single word "춤춰" (Dance!), the stick figure danced. The last step is dressing this skeleton as a person. Assistant, ready?

Colab code — run this page yourself

Both code notebooks use only libraries preinstalled in Colab. After "Download notebook (.ipynb)", open it in Colab via File → Upload notebook, or copy the code and paste it into a new notebook cell.

Code 1 · Bag of words and contrastive learning — words and motions on the same mapLinked to Sections 2–4 · numpy · about 5 s on CPU

Adds the dancing scene, turns sentences into a bag of words and motions into 16 numbers, then aligns the two funnels with contrastive learning. Prints the loss at each training step and the hits for the test sentences. To use your own data put description sentences for your motions in CAPTIONS and the word pieces to use in VOCAB.

Code 2 · Type words, get a motion — find, make, stitchLinked to Section 5 · numpy · about 5 s on CPU

Uses the two trained funnels to find or newly make a motion from a sentence, and stitches sentences joined with "~다가" (while …) one after the other. Judges the kind of each generated motion in the latent space. The table in Section 5 is built directly from this output.

Glossary

D

Analogy collection — and where the analogies break

Analogies are a first step toward understanding, but they can also plant misconceptions. Analogies to human perception are marked by strength. Direct there is evidence that it actually does the same thing · Partial only some properties are similar · None no known counterpart

ConceptEveryday analogyHuman perception analogyWhere the analogy breaks
Bag of wordsCutting a sentence into word cards, putting them in a bag and shaking itNoneCards taken out of the bag have no order. "The dog bites the man" and "The man bites the dog" become the same
Contrastive learningA pair-matching card game: stick matching pairs together, pull the others apartPartly a child who learns what words mean by hearing them while watching the actionA child learns in a few tries, but a model has to see the same pair hundreds of times, and a word with no pair stays unknown forever
Same mapPutting two languages together in one dictionaryNoneIn a dictionary, people decide the correspondences, but on this map the correspondences emerge from pair data alone. Words with few pairs end up in the wrong place
Find vs. makeBorrowing a book from a library vs. reading similar books and writing something newNoneNew writing has the author’s intent behind it, but “make” in this part only draws something near the average of the five nearest scenes
StitchingChoreography instructions like "first do ~, then do ~"Partly moving the body in the order of the sentenceA choreographer makes the transitions flow naturally, but here we simply blend 10 frames

Tips for educators

A teaching guide for instructors, on-the-job (OJT) trainers and tutors. Times are estimates, so adjust them to your actual class.

AudienceUniversity students and working adults who have finished 5-3. Planners and practitioners who want to know what goes on inside generative AI where "you type a prompt and get a result"
PrerequisitesThe latent space from 5-3; dot product and softmax (3-2, 3-8)
Learning goals① Explain the simplest way to turn a sentence into numbers (bag of words) and its limits ② Describe how contrastive learning aligns two funnels by "partners close, strangers far" ③ Give examples of the difference between find, make and stitch on a shared map
Estimated timeReading 30–40 min · animation demos 25 min · Colab practice 25 min (Code 1 12 min, Code 2 13 min)

Top 5 common misconceptions

MisconceptionCorrect explanationScene to show
AI understands the meaning of a sentence and then picks a motionIt only turns the sentence into numbers and finds a nearby spot on the map. In this part, the numbers only record whether each word piece is presentSection 2, Section 6
Contrastive learning needs answer labelsAll it needs are pairs saying "this sentence and this motion go together". Kind names are not usedSection 3, explanation
If the training loss is close to 0, it will also get unseen sentences rightThe loss is measured on training sentences. Only 5 of the 7 test sentences were rightSection 3 table
Longer, more detailed sentences always work betterIf words outside the dictionary or words from other motions creep in, the sentence can get dragged somewhere completely wrongSection 6, "손을 펴서 떨어뜨리고 걸어간다" (opens the hand, drops it and walks away)
"Make" creates entirely new motions that were not in the training dataIt draws near the spot where nearby scenes on the map gather. It can hardly go beyond the kinds of motion it learnedSection 5, "날아올라" (Fly up!)

Check questions (click to expand the answers)

Q1. If the dictionary has four slots [캔, 던지, 흔들, 손] (can, throw, wave, hand), what is the bag of words for "손을 흔들며 캔을 던진다" (throws a can while waving a hand)?

[1, 1, 1, 1]. All four pieces are in it. This sentence ends up somewhere between throwing and waving.

Q2. If the pair score table is [[3, 1], [0, 2]], what are the softmax probabilities of the first row? How does training try to change this row?

e³ / (e³ + e¹) ≈ 0.881, e¹ / (e³ + e¹) ≈ 0.119. Training adjusts the two funnels to push the diagonal (0.881) toward 1 and the non-pair cell (0.119) toward 0.

Q3. Why is test motion → sentence 100% while test sentence → motion is only 5 out of 7?

On the motion side there are 420 scenes, so each kind has a well-defined shape; on the sentence side there are only 3 training sentences per kind, and the bag of words does not know context. When an unseen combination of words comes in, the text funnel wobbles.

Q4. Why did the first half of "걷다가 손 흔들기" (walking, then waving) come out wrong?

"걷" (walk) is in the dictionary but never appeared in a training sentence. The weights for that slot are still the small random values they started with, so it does not point anywhere meaningful on the map. Change it to "걸어가다가" (while walking) and walking past comes out.

Q5. Which carries a greater privacy risk, find or make? Why?

Find. It pulls out training scenes as they are, so if they were real people’s motion data, that person’s movements would come out unchanged (like generator C in 5-2). Make draws something new from the spot where several scenes gather.

Colab assignments

Basic

In Code 1’s CAPTIONS, change one of the throwing training sentences to something similar to "길에 캔을 던져 버린다" (throws a can away on the street) and retrain. Report how the test-sentence hits change.

Challenge

Instead of the bag of words, write a bag function that uses "overlapping two-character pieces" (e.g. "던져" → "던", "져", "던져"), and compare by test-sentence hits whether it handles unseen words ("걷다가", while walking) better.
